item.title: SCP-5936:
item.content:encoded:
Minor nitpick - there are no such Polish names as "Damien", "Herbert" or "Annie" (there is "Damian" and "Ania" though, "Herbert" could be replaced by "Henryk" if you want it to sound more Polish). Also, "Tysiąclecie Górne" sounds rather unnatural for a name of district or village, but technically isn't incorrect, so it may be just me.

The last map suggests that there are going to be at least four more skips and/or tales set in Poland - as a Pole I can provide you with proof-reading if you want to, y'know, "polish" them before. (sorry for lame pun)

item.title: Tales of the Ethics Committee: The Foundation Eats Babies:
item.content:encoded:
Fantastic. Characters seem human and have different personalities. Little things like them nodding instead of verbally affirming in the beginning really sells it.

Also, my wife just finished her first trimester. This is our first pregnancy after years of fertility treatments. Makes this hit EXTRA hard for me, in good way. Well, I mean, not in a pleasant way, but in a powerful way.

item.title: SCP-2845:
item.content:encoded:
It was this time of year two years ago when the youtube algorithm randomly pushed me into learning about SCP, this was one of the articles that definitely helped push past my initial impression of "Oh, so it's some /x-y, murder-monster fan-fic site". Two years and, I dunno, like hundred articles read and it's still one of my favorites. Coming back to re-read it to get in the winter solstice spirit.

That said, the one thing that bothers me about this is the frequency of the ritual. The castration? Sure, big deal. The baby-eating? Yeah, super disturbing, kinda forces you to head-canon clone use for it as a fresh supply of infants seems even less likely than infinite D-class resources. But both those things become comically unrealistic when looking at that time frame. Personally, I would've tweaked it so it only needed to happen once a year during the winter solstice/Saturnalia season. Even the Yule-Man takes the summers off.

But that's just me. I don't expect any changes, that would be ridiculous, it's just my personal opinion. Also, I really want to know what the "hamfisted" ending that everyone was complaining about in the beginning was…. I feel like I should know how to look at previous edits but I still can't figure it out and at this point I'm too embarrassed to ask

item.title: Hear those Slay-Bells ring-a-ling:
item.content:encoded:
And here we have my first foray into tale writing and into horror.

Admittedly, the length kind of got away from me, but overall I like it. Although I think that while I was aiming for 'unknowable supernatural horror', I may have strayed closer to 'generic slasher' but… hey, if movies like "Black Christmas" can become cult classics, maybe this can too?
